content.text: I've reviewed the entire agreement. No MFN, "no less favourable terms," or price-matching provision exists anywhere.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: This rule is a direction test: the preferred position is that the Customer bears no most-favoured-nation obligation. A full read of the Agreement (single Preamble section, paragraphs p0000–p0074) shows no MFN, "no less favourable terms", benchmarking or third-party price-matching provision in either direction. The Fees and Payment clause (p0023) is a pure revenue-share referring to the Exhibits and imposes no obligation on AP to extend Kubient the best terms given to any other agent or platform. Clause 1 (p0001) reinforces this by expressly disclaiming exclusivity and preserving AP's right to offer Inventory through other agents or sell to third parties, which is the opposite of an MFN burden on us. Accordingly the Agreement sits at the preferred position and no redline is warranted. Note for the file: because pricing sits in the Exhibits, any Exhibit or later amendment should be checked for an MFN or "most favourable rates" undertaking running against AP; a Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would of course be welcome.
